Address.description: A single email address with an optional display name.

Envelope.description: A message summary, enough to list without fetching a body.

date.description:
The author-claimed send time, from the `Date:` header, `None` when
it is missing or unparseable.

flags.description:
The flags set on the message, a sorted set since wire order means
nothing and a duplicate is nonsense.

has-attachment.description:
Whether the message carries an attachment, `None` when the caller
did not ask or the backend cannot tell.

id.description:
The identifier the backend knows the message by: an IMAP UID, a
JMAP email id, a Maildir filename id.

in-reply-to.description:
The messages this one replies to, from its `In-Reply-To:` header.

A list, the grammar being `1*msg-id`. Each id is normalised like
[`Envelope::message_id`], so a client pairs a reply with its parent
from a listing alone.

message-id.description:
The RFC 5322 section 3.6.4 `Message-ID:`, normalised so it is
stable across every backend storing the message.

size.description: The size of the raw RFC 5322 message, in bytes.

Flag.description: A flag attached to an envelope, keeping its wire spelling and IANA tag.

IanaFlag.description:
IANA-registered email keywords, per the canonical table at
<https://www.iana.org/assignments/imap-jmap-keywords/>.

Declaration order is the derived [`Ord`], which is what gives stable
per-keyword sorting.

oneOf.description: The message has been replied to.
The message is marked for attention.
The message is an unsent draft.

A sync verb rather than a flag to propagate.

Adapters round-trip `\Deleted` so single-side workflows behave,
but a sync translates it into a delete on the other side.
The message has been marked as not junk.
The message is a phishing attempt.
The message is marked as important.
A disposition notification has been sent for the message.

description: The `envelope list` output, a table of envelopes.

queued.description:
Messages staged for creation and not pushed yet, which have no id
and so no row.

Zero for every backend whose writes reach the server as they are
made.
